tasks.short: Operate mobile dispatch vehicles and equipment.

steps.what: Operate mobile dispatch vehicles on the shift.
Maintain the equipment on the dispatch vehicle.
Note the vehicle check the dispatcher finished.

tasks.design: The dispatcher operates the mobile dispatch vehicle and maintains its equipment. A short note records a check they have finished. The driving and the maintenance stay physical.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operating the vehicle was never a screen task. The check was sometimes written twice.
tasks.enabler_now: A note can be typed once after the check. It does not operate the vehicle.
tasks.still_hard: The vehicle, the radio in it, and the road still need a person.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher operates the vehicle and maintains the equipment.
tasks.altitude: Operating the vehicle and maintaining the equipment stay. The note of a finished check is a little shorter.

reach.learn: The check was done by the dispatcher with the vehicle

evidence.claim: A vehicle-check note can be stored after the dispatcher has finished the check. Operating the vehicle stays with the person.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the vehicle goes out and ends when the note is written. Driving and maintenance stay outside any screen step.
The note fields are vehicle id and what was checked. The dispatcher writes them after the check. No tracking of the person is added.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree.
Upkeep is small: the note uses the vehicle id that already exists.
unknowns: Whether this service still uses a mobile dispatch vehicle.
Whether a paper defect book must still be signed in the vehicle.
research_questions: Does this service still field a mobile dispatch vehicle?
Must a defect still be written in a book kept in the vehicle?

already_counted.description: Operating the vehicle stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: No tracking is added; the note uses the existing vehicle id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conservative case keeps driving and maintenance in full. The low end moves only the check note, and only if it is still written twice. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor alarms for fires and illegal entry.

steps.what: Show the alarm the panel already displays.
Monitor alarm systems through the shift.
Decide if it is a fire or an illegal entry.
Note the decision after the dispatcher has made it.

tasks.design: The panel already displays the alarm, and that display is not treated as saved work. The dispatcher monitors the systems and decides whether it is a fire or an illegal entry. A note records the decision. No tool detects or classes the emergency.
tasks.previous_blocker: The panel already showed the alarm. The dispatcher still had to decide what it was and write it down.
tasks.enabler_now: The existing panel remains the display. The note can be typed once after the decision.
tasks.still_hard: False alarms are common, and a fire and an illegal entry are not the same response.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher detects the emergency by watching and deciding. The panel does not class it.
tasks.altitude: Monitoring and the decision stay with the dispatcher. The panel's existing display is not a saving. The note of a decision they have made is a little shorter.

reach.task: Attend a fire or an entry
reach.learn: Go when the dispatcher has decided what the alarm is

evidence.claim: An alarm note can be stored after the dispatcher has decided what the panel is showing.
Classifying an emergency call, or setting its priority, would choose the response without the dispatcher. The dispatcher keeps that decision.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the panel shows an alarm and ends when the note is written. Dispatching units stays in its own task.
The note fields are alarm id and the decision the dispatcher made. The dispatcher produces the decision. The panel event is an existing display and is not a saving. No classifier is added.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree. The panel's display is existing system work.
Upkeep is zero on a classifier because none is added.
unknowns: How often these alarms are false.
Whether the panel already stores a code for fire versus entry. A code would still not be the decision.
research_questions: What share of these alarms are false?
Does the panel already label an alarm, and who is allowed to trust that label?

already_counted.description: Deciding fire or illegal entry stays inside that step

incremental.description: No classifier is added, so there is nothing new to keep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the panel label is often wrong, it saves nothing and the low end is the monitoring and the decision, which stay. The panel display is excluded either way. No tool classes the alarm. 16 percent is work the system already does and is not saved human labour. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Driving the dispatch vehicle stays physical. Watching alarms stays with the dispatcher, who decides whether it is a fire or an illegal entry. The panel's existing display is not counted as saved work.
reach: A field unit attends a fire or an entry when the dispatcher has decided what the alarm is
skills_to_grow: Deciding the alarm without a classifier
Keeping the vehicle check as a note after the drive, not instead of it
role.ambitious_version: Every alarm response starts from the dispatcher's decision, and the vehicle is still operated by a person.
